# Legacy, Niche, and Non-Traction Battery Chemistries

- Document Class: Reference
- Status: Active
- Date: 2026-05-10
- Category: Battery chemistry
- Scope: Battery chemistries relevant to mobility context but not mainstream BEV traction.
- Sources: `raw/research/2026-05-10-ev-battery-technologies/sources/10-legacy-niche-and-non-traction-chemistries.md`
- Related: `wiki/specs/ev-battery-technology-landscape.spec.md`

## Compiled Notes

LMO has historical and niche EV relevance, often as a blended or older chemistry, but lower energy density and aging limitations reduce its role as a standalone modern BEV chemistry.

LTO offers excellent cycle life, safety, low-temperature operation, and fast charging, but low energy density and higher cost make it better suited to buses, industrial vehicles, specialty duty cycles, and stationary storage than mainstream passenger EVs.

NiMH remains relevant for hybrids and older electrified vehicles but is not competitive for modern long-range BEVs.

Lead-acid remains relevant for auxiliary low-voltage systems but not traction packs.

Metal-air, redox-flow, and iron-air technologies are more relevant to grid, range-extension concepts, or specialty systems than passenger BEV traction.

## Practical Boundary

Residual-value analysis for passenger EVs should focus on LFP/LMFP, NMC/NCA/NMCA, LMR, sodium-ion, silicon-enhanced lithium-ion, semi-solid, all-solid-state, lithium-metal, and lithium-sulfur.
